name: Texas utility-scale solar plants with replacement value and local hail exposure

plant_list.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Forms EIA-860 and EIA-860M, as processed by Catalyst Cooperative's Public Utility Data Liberation project (PUDL)
plant_list.licence: EIA data: U.S. government work. PUDL: CC BY 4.0 (per PUDL documentation; not re-checked here)
plant_list.citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Forms EIA-860 and EIA-860M, as processed by Catalyst Cooperative's Public Utility Data Liberation project (PUDL)

polygons.source: Fujita, K.S., et al., United States Large-Scale Solar Photovoltaic Database (USPVDB), U.S. Geological Survey and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory data release
polygons.licence: U.S. government work (public domain); attribution requested

value.source: NREL Annual Technology Baseline (ATB) 2025, electricity, v1.0.0
value.capacity_basis: per kW AC, as ATB reports utility PV
value.dollar_year: as stated in the ATB 2025 documentation; not given in the data file
value.rule: value_usd = capacity_ac_mw x 1000 x occ_usd_per_kw; replacement cost today, the same cost year for every plant

hail_exposure.label: N100-r10-75-A25
hail_exposure.region: Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Arkansas, Louisiana
hail_exposure.source: NOAA NCEI Storm Events, cleaned by crc-lab (Phase 2); neighbouring states from the same snapshot

return_levels: hail (mm) and gust (m/s) at the plant centroid from the Phase 3 curves via for_assets; return periods 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100
known_limits: Report-based hail: rates follow where people report. A minimum radius limits, but does not remove, that bias.
The footprint that turns a report rate into a chance at the plant is a placeholder with no source.
Value is a national benchmark cost per kW AC times capacity, not the plant's own cost or insured value.
The circle counts reports in Texas and its four neighbouring states and is clipped to them: there are no reports from Mexico or the Gulf.
Plants are EIA plants; most 2025-2026 plants have no polygon yet, so their area is estimated from capacity.
A plant is a disc of its USPVDB array area; the chance of a hit uses a disc of footprint plus plant radius.
